short_description: Consumer-facing nutrition trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal related to tea-intake tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing nutrition trait with workable raw-array support and a clear interpretation boundary between inherited tendency and real-world beverage habits.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with a tendency toward higher or lower tea intake, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Tea intake is presented here as a cautious relative nutrition signal, not a direct readout of your current daily tea or caffeine intake. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic readout of current tea intake, caffeine intake, hydration, or medical advice.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.
Real-world tea intake depends strongly on culture, region, household habits, caffeine tolerance, work routine, health advice, and beverage availability.
This trait should not be treated as a hydration assessment, caffeine-sensitivity result, or dietary recommendation.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from staged raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
